assets.name: walk
assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: transparent animation sprite sheet for the in-game pet 뚱땅. The attached image is the FINAL APPROVED character design and the STRICT pixel-art style reference. Draw this exact same compact fluffy blue-merle Pomeranian, with white forehead blaze/muzzle/chest/short paws, gray charcoal merle patches, tan cheeks and eyebrow patches, small icy-blue eyes, black pink-flecked nose, fluffy curled tail. Preserve every marking and the character proportions in every frame. No clothes, collar, accessories, invented features. Match the approved sprite's big connected pixel clusters, restrained palette and simple 2–3-tone shading. Real old MapleStory pet sprite art, native approximately 48 pixels of character height, nearest-neighbor enlarged for the preview. No painting, gradients, fine fur noise, 3D, motion blur, lighting changes, color shifts or resampling-only illusion.
Make a professional sprite sheet with THREE equal columns and TWO equal rows, SIX fully separate full-body sprites on genuinely transparent alpha. Read order left to right, then top to bottom. All cells use exactly the same camera, scale, head size, canvas size, character center and floor baseline. Leave generous empty transparent space between frames; no touching neighbors; nothing clipped. The dog occupies approximately 75 percent of each square cell. No labels, text, frame lines, checkerboard, background, floor or shadow. Animation: natural six-frame WALK LEFT cycle in clear side-to-three-quarter left view, not walking toward camera. Short legs alternate diagonal pairs with visible paw lift and forward reach, round torso rocks very subtly as it trots '뚱땅뚱땅'. A happy open mouth with small pink tongue and bright blue eyes throughout. Crucially the curled fluffy tail SWAYS naturally across all six frames: one side, halfway, middle, other side, halfway, middle, with a flexible base, not a rigid tail copied in every pose. Stable face markings and fur color. Leftmost frame begins the gait and sixth joins first smoothly. Four-leg anatomy remains clear, no detached paws or extra legs. This is a joyful plodding Pomeranian dog, not an anthropomorphic character.
